messages:
sam: Quick thread — I ran a focused perf/telemetry run comparing routing decisions (Triton vs CUTLASS) on h100 with autotune enabled. High-level: p90/p99 tail spikes at seq_len=1024 when Triton was picked. Correlates with KV-cache miss bursts. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/run-2026-03-kvtest (run-2026-03-kvtest).

maria: Can you drop the probe config and batch matrix? what were warmup/steady-state settings?

sam: Probe config pasted below:
```yaml
model: redwood-7b
seq_lengths: [256, 512, 1024]
batches: [1, 4, 8]
autotune: true
probe_plan: 'kv-hotpath'
warmup_requests: 50
metrics: [latency, kv_miss_ratio, kernel_score]
```
KV-cache warmup=50 reqs. Observed KV miss ratio jump at 1024 when Triton chosen — miss spikes coincide with decision flips.

kevin: Was the routing decision switching mid-request (i.e., kernel fallback) or per-request? mid-request fallback is dangerous for KV coherency.

sam: It's per-request routing but we saw many back-to-back requests on the same shard taking different paths (flip-flop). Hysteresis is 0.15 right now. Logs sample:
```
[2026-03-16T14:12:03Z] shard-3 decision: TRITON score=0.62, CUTLASS score=0.59 -> choose TRITON
[2026-03-16T14:12:03Z] shard-3 kv: miss -> trigger remote fetch
[2026-03-16T14:12:03Z] shard-3 decision: fallback to CUTLASS after timeout
```
Observability shows KV misses then a fallback; that sequence is what creates spikes.

anya: @sam can you share probe latency distribution? If probe latency crosses threshold we may trigger fallback incorrectly.

sam: Probe latencies for seq_len=1024: median=4.2ms, p90=12.1ms, p99=78ms. When probe>40ms we hit the fallback path. Fallback policy: 10ms soft-decision window + 100ms hard timeout.

maria: The autotuner scoring may overweight microbenchmark throughput/p99 and ignore KV-miss penalty. That would explain picking kernels that win raw gen perf but are KV-unfriendly. We should add KV-sensitivity into scoring.

kevin: +1. Proposal: score' = base_score - alpha * kv_miss_cost_est, where kv_miss_cost_est = avg_remote_fetch_ms * expected_miss_rate. alpha tunable per model/seq-len. Also make the score sequence-length-aware.

sam: Did a quick alpha sweep. With alpha=0.7 Triton picks at seq_len=1024 dropped by ~60% and p99 improved ~18%. Artifact: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/run-2026-03-kvtest/alpha07

ci-bot: CI: profile artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/run-2026-03-kvtest/alpha07

anya: Next steps I propose: 1) bake KV-sensitivity into autotuner scoring; 2) move hysteresis state to per-shard sticky state instead of per-request to avoid flip-flopping under bursty traffic; 3) reduce fallback hard timeout from 100ms -> 60ms on hotpath.

maria: Also consider adding a KV-prefetch hint when Triton is chosen. For seq_len 1024 we can async pre-warm expected KV indices when batch size>1. Prefetch costs ~1.2ms median but reduces miss rate ~40% in my microbench.

sam: Confirmed — prefetch tradeoff: +1.2ms median overhead vs -40% miss rate and ~12-14% p99 improvement in heavy traffic. Recommend behind a per-customer flag initially.

kevin: I'll prototype the KV-penalty term and per-shard hysteresis. Can we canary this quickly? @anya can you reserve a small h100 pool?

anya: Reserved pool 'kv-canary-1' tomorrow 10:00-12:00. Added canary config to Console and set traffic split 5%.

maria: One more thing from flamegraphs: we saw a memcopy hotspot when falling back from Triton -> CUTLASS due to layout differences (transpose/align). If we standardize KV buffer layout across kernel backends we can avoid copies. That might reduce fallback pain.

sam: Good catch. I'll open a PR to normalize KV buffer layout across the kernel interface and re-run alpha=0.7 after the layout fix.

kevin: Creating tracking issue and will attach artifacts + plan.

sam: Tracking: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3210 — links to runs and proposed autotuner patch.

maria: TL;DR: add KV-awareness to autotuner, prefer per-shard stickiness, prefetch hints + layout normalization. Preliminary alpha=0.7 looks promising.

kevin: Thanks everyone. We'll iterate on the canary results tomorrow and decide if this becomes default autotuner behavior. :thumbsup:
